target.renderPrompt:
Edit this photo of a room in our house. Keep the exact camera angle and keep all the architecture exactly as it is — walls, room shape, windows, doors, beams, floor and fixed fittings. Do not add, move or remove anything structural, and do not change the furniture unless I say so below. Remove all clutter: tools, boxes, bags, dust sheets, loose cables, packaging, laundry and toiletries. Show the room finished and tidy.

Changes to make:
- Keep everything already there: the black-framed sliding shower, dark shower tray, black shower fittings, blush vertical tiles, grey stone-effect tiles, white WC, small square basin with black tap, pink ceiling and the disco ball.
- The WC sits tight against the wall with neat grey tiling behind it — no visible pipe or hole.
- The row of glass blocks at the top of the wall is gone, replaced by the same grey stone-effect tiles running up to the ceiling.
- A small white extractor fan grille high on the wall.
- The door is a white panelled sliding pocket door, full height, with a flush black pull, in a neatly finished white frame.

Style: photorealistic interior photograph, natural light plus warm 2700K lamps, no people, no text or labels.

scope: Job 1: make good behind the WC so no pipe or hole is visible
Job 2: tile over the glass blocks on the bathroom side
Job 3: finish the door surround and supply/fit a sliding door 210 cm high

surfaces.prep: Pull the pan forward; check the waste connection is sound and sealed. Fit a shorter/straight pan connector so the pan sits tight to the wall; cut in a tile patch (same grey tile) or neat collar to close the rough hole.
surfaces.finish: Re-fix pan, silicone bead (white, sanitary) pan-to-wall and pan-to-floor
surfaces.notes: If no spare tile: a white or black pipe collar/rosette plus silicone is the fallback

surfaces.surface: Glass-block row above door, bathroom side (Job 2)
surfaces.prep: Glass is non-porous — tiles will not bond to it directly. Either (a) apply a grip primer for non-absorbent surfaces, or (b, more reliable) fix a thin tile-backer board over the blocks. Rake out and fill the mortar joints flush first.
surfaces.finish: Tile to the ceiling with flexible (S1) adhesive; grout to match
surfaces.colour: Grey stone-effect tile, to match the rest of that wall (decided)
surfaces.notes: Tiling over removes the borrowed daylight: the room will rely fully on artificial light and needs a working extractor fan

surfaces.prep: Square up and plaster the broken reveal and both faces round the opening; fit a timber or plaster lining and architraves each side; make good the wall above the track
surfaces.finish: Paint surround to match walls; door in warm white eggshell
surfaces.notes: Pocket door (slides inside the wall). Opening 74 cm wide, height 210 cm. The pocket is only about 66 cm deep, so the door never fully disappears — about 60 cm clear opening when open; accepted. Leaf to order: 75 × 210 cm, panelled, painted warm white, with FLUSH pulls both sides and an edge pull (projecting handles cannot enter the pocket). The old door is too short and its brass handles project — keep the handles for reuse elsewhere.

surfaces.prep: Core a 100 mm hole through an outside wall (or duct through the ceiling/roof), with an external grille and backdraught shutter. Electrician to wire it with a run-on timer (or humidity sensor) so it keeps running after the light goes off.
surfaces.finish: Quiet fan rated for bathroom zones (IP44 or better), black or white cover to suit the room
surfaces.notes: Do this BEFORE tiling over the glass blocks and painting, so cable and duct routes are hidden. Decide the position on site: high on the wall, as far from the door as possible, not inside the shower spray

notes: Do not disturb the shower enclosure, tray, tiles or fittings
Other side of the glass blocks (fridge & utility room): to be plastered over — see that room
Order: fan first-fix → tiling over glass blocks → WC → door
brief.access: Room in daily use — agree working days
